e-5387.knowledge_point: Finding the Intersection of a Polar Circle With an Axis
e-5387.problem: Find the **polar** coordinates of the point where the polar curve $r=2.7$ intersects the negative $x$-axis.
e-5387.worked_solution:
The polar curve $r=2.7$ is a circle of radius $2.7$ centered at the origin. It crosses the negative $x$-axis at the point where $r=2.7$ and $\theta = \pi.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13959689/assets/04f57721c8672bf48aa6f07bf6c9571f826ab957d104a40b273254b4f50ff147.png)

Therefore, the point of intersection in polar coordinates is $\left(2.7, \pi\right).$

e-5388.knowledge_point: Finding the Polar Equation of a Circle Given a Point on the Circumference
e-5388.problem:
Find the polar equation of the circle centered at the origin that passes through the point $A(2,5)$, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13959689/assets/063df02b7846c476657a2deaa00937967707472a97b0e52a4a8b3dc5951ce1ab.png)
e-5388.worked_solution:
A circle of radius $k$ centered at the origin has the polar equation $r = k.$

We can compute the radius $k$ of our circle using the Pythagorean theorem, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}k & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{5}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{29}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the circle is $r=\sqrt{29}.$

after.name: Question 11
after.problem: Find the polar equation of the circle that is centered at the origin and that passes through the point $A(-5,-3).$
after.worked_solution:
A circle of radius $k$ centered at the origin has the polar equation $r=k.$

We can compute the radius $k$ of our circle using the Pythagorean theorem, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}k & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-5)^{2}+(-3)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{34}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the circle is $r=\sqrt{34}.$

after.worked_solution:
A circle of radius $k$ centered at the origin has the polar equation $r=k.$

$$
